buffer: 20 mM Tris·HCl pH 8.0, 0.5 mM EDTA, 5–10 mM DTT, 150 mM NaCl, 7% D2O, 0.7 mM DSS, 0.02% sodium azide
experiment: 15N-HSQC at 600/800 MHz showing two sets of signals (two Trp side-chain peaks) and 2D 1H-15N exchange spectrum (60 ms mixing time, 750 MHz Bruker in Methods; 600 MHz in the Fig. 1E legend)
other_conditions: regime (authors): two states interchange slowly on the NMR time scale; ordered state resembles Zn-IscU; exchange cross peaks mainly in helices alpha3 and alpha4; exchange-linked residues D24-G28, G51-E54, L82-K89, D92-L97 (Table S1, not in text); related structures: 1R9P (H. influenzae Zn-IscU, homolog)
residues_author: D24-G28, G51-E54, L82-K89, D92-L97; W76 (side-chain peaks)
timescale: state lifetimes = ms–s range (2D exchange); interconversion rates x and y slower than 10 s−1 (separate signals for the two states) but faster than 0.3 s−1 (2D exchange peaks) (Fig. 7 legend bounds)
population: two states have nearly equal populations (Fig. 7 legend); helix α3 in the disordered state populated at about 33–50% and helix α4 at about 25–33% (secondary-structure content of the disordered state from Cα-Cβ shifts, not state populations)
author_claim: Wild-type apo-IscU exists as an ordered and a largely disordered conformation interconverting on the ms–s timescale; helices alpha3 and alpha4 undergo exchange between ordered structure and a random-coil-like conformation.
anchor: This result confirmed that these two peaks originate from two exchanging conformations, rather than two covalently distinct protein species, and indicated that the two states have lifetimes in the ms–s range.
locator: Results, Two Interconverting Conformational States of Apo-IscU (Fig. 1A, 1E, Fig. 2); Fig. 7 legend for rates; conditions: Experimental Procedures
caveat_note: Wild-type, not the D39A deposit sample. The exchange field is 750 MHz in Methods but 600 MHz in the Fig. 1E legend. The x and y bounds are the authors' inference from signal-observation arguments in a cartoon legend, not fitted rates.

buffer: 20 mM Tris·HCl pH 8.0, 3 mM ZnCl2, 5–10 mM DTT, 150 mM NaCl, 7% D2O, 0.7 mM DSS, 0.02% sodium azide (no EDTA listed)
experiment: 15N-HSQC of apo-IscU with and without 3 mM ZnCl2 at 600/800 MHz
other_conditions: regime (authors): slow exchange between ordered and disordered states; related structures: 1R9P
residues_author: C37, G38, V40-L43, G62, C63, S69-S71, V73, T74, K89, N90, C106-L109, E111-A113, K115, A117 (largest differences between Zn-IscU and apo-IscU(D39A))
population: zinc shifts the equilibrium so that broad signals of the disordered state and the minor Trp peak disappear (qualitative, no percentages)
author_claim: Zinc binding removes the disordered-state signals while the ordered-state peaks remain, so zinc or D39A stabilizes the ordered conformation.
anchor: The addition of ZnCl 2 caused the broad and overlapped signals in the center of the HSQC spectrum to disappear while most sharp and dispersed peaks were retained without significant peak shifts
locator: Results, Two Interconverting Conformational States of Apo-IscU (Fig. 1B, 1D)
caveat_note: Metal-bound wild-type sample, not the deposit. The residue list is the set of residues that differ between Zn-IscU and apo-IscU(D39A) spectra, mostly metal-binding or Zn-ordered regions.

buffer: 20 mM Tris·HCl pH 8.0, 0.5 mM EDTA, 5–10 mM DTT, 150 mM NaCl, 7% D2O, 0.7 mM DSS, 0.02% sodium azide
experiment: 15N-HSQC of apo-IscU(D39A) compared with apo-IscU at 600/800 MHz
construct_or_mutation: E. coli IscU(D39A), 0.8 mM [U-15N] (2.5 mM [U-13C,U-15N] for assignments)
other_conditions: regime (authors): D39A shifts the ordered/disordered equilibrium toward the ordered state; related structures: 1R9P
population: peaks of the less structured state become very weak relative to the more structured conformation (qualitative)
author_claim: D39A stabilizes the ordered state of IscU and is used as a surrogate for the folded state; unassigned residues are mainly N-terminal or metal-binding loops.
anchor: Thus, the D39A substitution shifts the equilibrium between the ordered and disordered states of IscU rather than altering its secondary or tertiary structure.
locator: Results, Two Interconverting Conformational States of Apo-IscU and Resonance Assignments of Apo-IscU(D39A) (Fig. 1C); conditions: Experimental Procedures
caveat_note: Matches the deposit on temperature (25 °C), pH 8.0 and 600 MHz; the sample buffer matches the card (Tris, DTT, EDTA, NaCl, azide). Residue range S69-L99 etc. reflects assigned residues, not dynamic residues.

buffer: 20 mM Tris·HCl pH 8.0, 0.5 mM EDTA, 5–10 mM DTT, 150 mM NaCl, 7% D2O, 0.7 mM DSS, 0.02% sodium azide
experiment: 15N R1, R2 and 1H-15N heteronuclear NOE at 600 MHz (two replicate sets)
other_conditions: mean R1 = 1.64 (±0.26) s−1, mean R2 = 15.37 (±3.90) s−1, mean NOE = 0.73 (±0.29); regime (authors): ps–ns dynamics (high R1, low NOE) for K6-D9, D21, N22, C37, G38, A39; simultaneous ps–ns and µs–ms dynamics for F58-K59, G62, C63, S69-S71; slow (µ–ms) exchange for L97-L99, I108, L109; related structures: 1R9P
author_claim: Apo-IscU(D39A) is ordered with ps–ns flexibility in termini and metal-binding loops and µs–ms exchange in the C-terminal region including the LPPVK motif (residues 99-103) that binds HscA.
anchor: Residues L97–L99, I108, and L109 had distinctively high R 2 values without either an increase in R 1 values or a decrease in 1 H- 15 N NOE
locator: Results, Backbone Dynamics of Apo-IscU(D39A) (Fig. 3); conditions: Experimental Procedures, NMR Spectroscopy

Residues T60, Y61, G64-A68 and M1-E5, H10-N13, N23, A36 were not observed, plausibly because of the dynamics the authors describe.

buffer: 20 mM Tris·HCl pH 8.0, 0.5 mM EDTA, 5–10 mM DTT, 150 mM NaCl, 7% D2O, 0.7 mM DSS, 0.02% sodium azide
experiment: 2D 15N-TROSY-HSQC titration of [U-15N]IscU(D39A) with unlabeled HscB (final HscB:IscU ratio 2) at 600 MHz
ligand_or_partner: HscB (2.5 mM stock aliquots), final molar ratio HscB:IscU 2
other_conditions: regime (authors): rearrangement within the IscU:HscB complex much faster than dissociation, causing broadening at substoichiometric HscB; Kd ≅ 10 µM (ITC, Fig. S1); related structures: 1R9P
timescale: rearrangement in the IscU:HscB complex faster than complex dissociation (no value fitted); model rates in Fig. 7 are approximations from Kd ≅ 10 µM, an assumed association rate of 10 7 s−1 and assumed chemical shift differences of about 0.5 ppm (300 / 400 s−1 for 1H at 600 / 800 MHz)
population: HscB binds the ordered state of apo-IscU and stabilizes it (qualitative); complex exists as two (or more) interconverting states
author_claim: HscB binds the ordered state and stabilizes it; the most perturbed regions are the two N-terminal beta strands and the C-terminal alpha helix; the extreme line broadening at substoichiometric HscB requires a dynamic rearrangement of the bound complex faster than dissociation.
anchor: These peaks disappeared from the HSQC spectrum at an HscB:IscU ratio of ∼0.4.
locator: Results, Perturbations in the Chemical Shifts of Apo-IscU(D39A) upon Addition of HscB (Fig. 4A); Discussion and Fig. 7 legend
caveat_note: Liganded sample, not the deposit. The rearrangement model (shuffling of hydrophobic contacts or two orientations) is a hypothesis; the Fig. 7 rates are labelled crude estimates built on assumed values, not measurements. Interconverting complex states are not structurally identified.
